# Status pill — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for the status pill when a status needs one line: the one-line status label on the tone registry. `tone` picks one of the seven registry tones in container roles by default, so light, dark and contrast modes follow with no conditionals, while the solid emphasis fills with the tone roles for counts that must read at a glance and soft stays the quiet default. `icon` takes a registry node and hides the dot, and `dot` forces the dot off when the icon carries the meaning; compact density fits table status-chip cells while medium is the default row height. A pill marks and never activates — there is no click or action, because a status that navigates is a link or a button — there is no hex or utility colour, because a status with no registry tone is an addendum rather than a local override, and there is no truncation prop: the label is the host's string, so keep it to a word or two.

## Native

### Features

Reach for the status pill when a status needs one line: the one-line status label on the tone registry — the native twin under the same contract. `tone` picks one of the seven registry tones in container roles by default, so light, dark and contrast modes follow with no conditionals, while the solid emphasis fills with the tone roles for counts that must read at a glance and soft stays the quiet default. `icon` takes a registry node and hides the dot, and `dot` forces the dot off when the icon carries the meaning; compact density fits table status-chip cells while medium is the default row height. A pill marks and never activates — there is no press action, because a status that navigates is a link or a button — there is no hex or utility colour, because a status with no registry tone is an addendum rather than a local override, and there is no truncation prop: the label is the host's string, so keep it to a word or two.
